title: Onboard Cognitive Load Minimizer — 7-Day Quiet Launch Checklist for Engineers
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, pragmatic 7-day onboarding checklist for new engineers that intentionally minimizes cognitive load during week 0/1. Goals: keep context switching low, protect deep work windows, ensure safe ramping of responsibilities, and give mentors a clear micro-schedule.

Scope:
- Target: ICs joining product, infra, and platform squads (first contributor week).
- Mode: remote-first, supports hybrid.
- Not a replacement for role-specific runbooks; links to those are included.

Principles (short):
1) Default to fewer meetings: limit scheduled orientation to 3 short touchpoints across Day 0–3.
2) Surface one clear deliverable per day (micro-goal).
3) Schedule 90–120 minute deep work blocks each afternoon for onboarding tutorials and code reading.
4) Mentor-led 30-minute micro-sessions rather than long sit-downs.
5) Explicitly call out safety signals and escalation paths.

Pre-Day 0 (HR + Eng setup checklist — to be completed before first day):
- HR: contract signed, first-pay payroll setup confirmed.
- IT: laptop imaged and encrypted, hardware notes, manager-approved hardware request completed.
- Access: GitHub org invite sent, Google account provisioned, Jira and Confluence access granted.
- Workspace: Slack channel created (#onboard-<name>), calendar stub created with 3 orientation slots (all optional with default no).
- Pre-read: short 30–45 minute "what-we-build" doc emailed (link) + architecture diagram + top 5 code reading pointers.

Day 0 (welcome, low-bandwidth):
- Micro-goal: confirm local dev environment builds (or at least runs smoke script).
- Slack: intro post template (people-ops owner) to announce arrival. Keep message one paragraph.
- Manager: 20-min sync to set expectations and agree on 7-day quiet-launch plan.
- Mentor: 30-min meet & greet (synchronous or async video) focused on immediate block schedule.
- No other meetings.

Day 1 (context + safety):
- Micro-goal: run a test change (tiny doc or README fix) and open a draft PR.
- Safety checks: confirm 2FA, password manager onboarding, and emergency contact details.
- Access: verify access to dev/staging infra read-only. If blocked, escalate to SRE oncall.
- 60–90 min deep work block: read main architecture doc + top 3 repos.
- 15-min mentor micro-session: questions and clarifications.

Day 2 (silent pairing + small contribution):
- Micro-goal: ship a tiny non-production code change with CI passing (or update a test case).
- Pairing: optional 1-hour shadowing with code owner (recording allowed for async review).
- No meetings after 3pm local time.

Day 3 (integrations + product):
- Micro-goal: understand deployment pipeline end-to-end and identify one low-risk improvement or doc edit.
- 30-min product overview (recorded) if role is product-facing. Otherwise optional.
- Mentor micro-session: review PR and deployment questions.

Day 4 (consumer loop):
- Micro-goal: triage one small ticket in backlog, add a comment and proposed next step.
- Observability: walkthrough of logs, tracing dashboard, and how to read a common failure.
- If production debugging access is required for task, pair with mentor and follow production access checklist.

Day 5 (first small independent ticket):
- Micro-goal: take ownership of a 1–2 day ticket (non-prod) and deliver a PR for review.
- 30-min review with reviewer scheduled at their convenience (no synchronous gating).
- Manager check-in: 20-min to reflect on week, surface blockers.

Day 6–7 (stabilize + reflect):
- Micro-goal: finish review feedback, confirm deploy steps, and propose next 30-day learning objectives.
- Create a 30-day plan draft in the onboarding tracker and share with manager.
- End-of-week async retrospective: 5-minute form (what went well, blockers, suggestions).

Default schedule rules (for the 7-day window):
- Meeting budget: max 3 scheduled syncs across Day0–3 (manager, mentor, HR) — all optional.
- Deep work: block 90–120 minutes daily between 13:00–16:00 local as uninterrupted onboarding window.
- Notification policy: Slack DND for the deep work window, except for paging channels (sre-paging).
- Code review expectations: reviewers should give initial feedback within 48 hours for "onboard" PRs.

Mentor playbook (30-min micro-sessions):
- 5 min: quick status + psychological safety check (how are you tracking load?).
- 10–15 min: focused walkthrough (code path, deployment step, or docs).
- 5–10 min: agree next micro-goal and experiments.
- Document the session in the onboarding tracker as a single line note.

Safety signals (immediate escalation triggers):
- Cannot get essential access after 24 hours -> escalate to access admin and manager.
- Recurrent blockers in CI for >2 days -> flag to team SRE and manager.
- New hire reports excessive confusion, anxiety, or repeated context loss -> people-ops check-in and temporary meeting cap.

Acceptance email template (short):
Subject: Welcome to Redwood — first steps
Body:
Hi <Name>,
Welcome! Quick actions for Day 0:
1) Confirm laptop arrival + imaging link
2) Sign into Google and Slack
3) Run the quick smoke script in the pre-read (link)
We’ve set a short manager sync and a mentor intro — everything else is optional. If anything’s blocked, reply to this thread and we’ll triage.
— People Ops

Onboarding PR label convention (helps reduce cognitive load):
- label: onboard/first-week -> automatic review priority and 48-hour review SLA.

Interview rubric snippet to inform hiring handoffs (compact):
- Problem decomposition: 1–4 scale with explicit examples asked.
- Communication: clear concision and ability to explain tradeoffs.
- Systems intuition: demonstrates mental model of service boundaries and failures.
- Culture fit: curiosity, pragmatic ownership.
Notes: Hiring debriefs should include explicit "expected Day 30 impact" to align ramp expectations.

Open questions / TODOs (working doc):
- Add localized calendar suggestions for APAC/EU hires (time zone friendly deep work windows).
- Create a lightweight "first PR walkthrough" recording template for mentors to reuse.
- Decide whether to gate some Day 5 tasks behind manager approval for high-risk infra teams.
- Map the onboarding tracker to the new HRIS fields (onboarding metadata).

Links & quick refs:
- Role runbook templates: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/role-templates
- Onboard tracker: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/ONBOARD-TRACKER
- Quiet launch policy doc: https://confluence.redwood/policies/quiet-launch

Feedback / revision log (short):
- 2025-10-28: draft created by Avery Chen.
- 2025-10-30: added mentor micro-session template (Jordan).
- 2025-11-04: clarified meeting budget and added safety signals (Maya).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc intentionally short and actionable. Avoid long role checklists; link out.
- Consider automated Slack nudges for DND deep work windows.
notes: This file is a working draft intended for People Ops and hiring managers; adapt for specific team constraints.
